title: 无题·相见时难
pinyin: Wú Tí · Xiāng Jiàn Shí Nán
englishTitle: Untitled: Hard to Meet, Hard to Part
author: Li Shangyin

translation: Meeting is hard, and parting is hard too
The east wind is feeble; a hundred flowers fade
The spring silkworm spins until it dies
The candle's tears dry only when it burns to ash
At dawn she fears the mirror shows her hair turning gray
Chanting at night, she must feel the moonlight's chill
Mount Penglai is not so far from here
May the blue bird fly faithfully to look upon you

annotations.春蚕: spring silkworm — a symbol of devotion; 丝 (silk) puns with 思 (longing)
annotations.蜡炬: candle — its dripping wax resembles tears
annotations.云鬓: cloud-like hair — a woman's beautiful hair
annotations.蓬山: Mount Penglai — a mythical island of immortals
annotations.青鸟: blue bird — the mythical messenger of the Queen Mother of the West

appreciation: Li Shangyin's untitled love poems are the most enigmatic in Chinese literature. The third and fourth lines — the silkworm spinning until death, the candle weeping until ash — became China's defining metaphor for undying devotion, later adopted to honor teachers. Every couplet is dense with wordplay and myth.
